subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for a crab model using the SDK, sketching real-world proportions—roughly 0.36m shell width and 0.12m height—and setting up a root body joint before deciding how to construct the shell geometry.

For the shell, I'm thinking of using a scaled sphere primitive to get a flattened carapace shape instead of a custom lathe. For the legs, rather than relying on inverse kinematics, I'm working out how to define explicit joint chains (hip, knee, ankle, tip) per leg, reasoning through how the naming convention maps to the number of points and joints in each chain.

I'm planning each leg as a tapered sweep through its chain, using a pointed cap for the tip spike, and positioning four legs per side along the body.

Legs will each have four points—hip, knee, ankle, tip—with the pointed cap extending slightly beyond the path end at the floor. For the claws, I'm planning an arm chain of shoulder, elbow, wrist joints on the raised side, with pincer pieces attached at the wrist using extruded crescent-shaped blades for the upper and lower jaws rather than simple capsules.

Writing claw sweep code...

Still writing claw geometry...

For the eye stalks, I'm attaching them from the body using a joint reference, building them as rods connecting two points with a sphere eyeball and pupil on top.

For the shell, I'm rooting the body joint, scaling a shell sphere, then scattering small bump spheres across its surface using a filtered random scatter and embedding them slightly for a knobbly texture. I'm planning a speckled paint pattern over the shell mixing brick red with orange and cream tones.

For extra detail, I want to add a barnacle by placing a small flattened shape on the shell's back using surface coordinates around its center, positioned toward the rear and slightly elevated.

Adding seaweed frond geometry...

For legs, I'm planning 8 legs total, 4 per side, each swept along a chain with a tapered radius and a darker red/brick color, with a pointed end cap.

I'm working out the joint naming scheme for each leg's chain (hip, knee, ankle, tip per side and index), making sure names avoid hyphens, and setting the root body joint as the parent for the leg chains.

Now I'm positioning the actual leg joint coordinates, calculating per-leg offsets for hip, knee, ankle, and tip based on side and index to give each leg a slightly different stance, and cross-checking these against the shell's scaled sphere dimensions so the legs attach sensibly at the body's edge.

I'm also working out the shell's bottom and top y-extents, then placing the eye stalks and claw arm coordinates (shoulder, elbow, wrist, pincer) so they protrude naturally from the shell surface at the front.

Building the arm chain and palm geometry...

Adjusting the jaw curves...

For the right claw, I'm keeping it smaller and simpler than the left—a short chain from shoulder to tip with basic pincer prongs rather than the full sweep geometry, just to keep it modest. I'll skip the mouth entirely and move on to the carapace, starting with a front shell piece.

I'm adding scattered ridge knobs on the shell using alternating cream and orange spheres, and locking in the full palette—brick, red, orange, cream, dark, green, leg-brown, barnacle. Then I'm applying spotted paint texture to the shell and solid color to the leg sweeps, with pointed caps on leg tips so they taper properly, and rounded caps where they tuck into the hips.

I'm tallying the part count—legs, shell, bumps, eye stalks, pupils, arms, pincers, teeth, palm, small claw—landing around eighty parts, which should be fine. I'm setting up the export metadata with a name and description, then starting the builder code with THREE and the createBuilder, rng, and spots helpers. I'm double-checking the signatures for part, stick, and surface functions to make sure scale, embed, and scatter options work as expected, then writing the barnacle placement logic using surface.around() with a null check since that call might return nothing.

Now I'm adding a second, smaller barnacle using a cone geometry stuck onto the shell surface, then working out where to place seaweed on the back of the shell using another surface point with a slightly different azimuth and elevation so it doesn't overlap the barnacles. I'm building the seaweed path with a catmull curve through a few offset points derived from the hit frame, making sure the frame-to-point conversion works correctly for the curve function.

Writing sprout and stalk code...

Then I'm adding the pupil and eye-white spheres with offset positions, defining a body joint at the root, and attaching the shell sphere to it scaled flatter and wider so it sits above the legs properly, keeping the geometry low-poly for simplicity.

Now I'm sketching the leg rig: looping over four leg pairs on each side, building named joint chains for hip, knee, ankle, and tip, then sweeping tapered tubes along catmull-rom curves through those joints for smooth leg shapes, and assigning a "leg" role to each chain for the rig system.

Moving on, I'm positioning the claw arm with its own joint chain from shoulder to wrist, sweeping a tapered tube for the forearm, then adding a flattened palm sphere at the wrist position. For the mouth, I'm building upper and lower jaw curves as catmull-rom paths that converge near the tip with a small gap, then sweeping tapered bands along them bound explicitly to the wrist bone to keep them anchored correctly.

Now I'm figuring out the teeth placement — spiking small cone shapes downward along the upper jaw path, but realizing the spike base needs to start from the outer edge of the tube rather than the centerline, so I'm working out how to offset the spike origin using the path frame's local axes so the teeth actually poke visibly out from the jaw surface instead of staying hidden inside it.

I'll pass an explicit bone (wristR/wristL) for clarity, then set up the lower teeth row with an upward-facing offset, small claws built from catmull-rom arm paths ending at wrist joints, short red pincer sweeps with dark caps, and a palm sphere pinned to the wrist bone. Then I'm scattering small cream/orange bump spheres across the shell surface, filtering by normal direction to avoid placing them on the underside.

I'm now placing a barnacle sprout on the shell using a surface-relative position, then building a seaweed sprout with a catmull-rom path that curves outward from a surface hit point along its local normal and tangent axes toward a tip position.

For the seaweed I'm adding a second frond at a different surface spot and a small sphere bulb at the tip for extra detail. Then I'm defining the joint hierarchy, naming the root "hips" with a "spine" role, and making sure chain and joint names across the whole skeleton (legs, arms, wrists, eye stalks) stay unique and consistent before returning the final root.

Now I'm working out the eye geometry — spheres for the eyeballs and smaller dark pupils positioned slightly in front — and setting up the shell's speckled coloring using a spots paint function layered with brick, orange, and cream tones to get that mottled look. I'm double-checking the imports needed (THREE, builder, rng, spots, catmull, offset) before finalizing the code.

For the legs, I'm looping through both sides and four leg positions, building each as a chain of curved points (hip, knee, ankle, tip) using catmull splines, with the front and back legs splayed at different angles so they look naturally posed. Then I'm sweeping a tapered tube along each leg path with rounded joints and a pointed toe cap, adjusting the tip position so it doesn't poke oddly below the body. Writing leg sweep code...
